method: An operator supplied two choice groups and a community reference. The live geometry agent returned six equipment operations. A later operator-directed arm revision used the public proposal importer, was accepted in the editor, and replayed the equipment on the new limbs. The two-arm control was derived by removing two complete branches and bending an elbow using the editor control.

plateGeneration.instructions: Keep this four-handed performer, their saved clothes, face, glasses and body. Give ONLY their pressure suit an original bulky hull inspired by the reference creature's repeated layers of tooth-like armour. Use the equipPlates operation on the existing body sweep for overlapping chest scales and back scales, and on four upper-arm sweeps for shoulder guards. Honour the drawn chest row count and shell colour. Keep individual shields broad enough to overlap and read at game size. Keep the face, hands and their range of movement clear. The chest should have three columns, covering the upper chest down to the midriff. Preserve every existing part as is. Use only additive equipPlates operations. Stay under 128 total parts. Make the stage clothes and practice layer exactly as they were.
plateGeneration.summary: Add a warm ivory pressure-suit hull with three-by-three overlapping tooth-like chest shields, layered back scales and subtly asymmetric guards on all four shoulders; preserve all existing parts and saved outfits.

limits: The sleeve below the cape still has a visible join. Screen-space overlap depends on camera and pose. Crossing counts cover opposite tiers on the same side, at twelve equally spaced samples per clip plus rest. The rear pack remains boxy. The likeness and garments are stylized.
